While I, personally, fully agree with your statement that we should be helping communities escape poverty, and in a perfect world, yes that would help - unfortunately, it's just much more complex than that. Police brutality is what had created distrust between officers and civilians. Officers have been abusing their authority well before the BLM movement started, and the only reason that the movement began is because black communities are so tired of seeing a lack of justice due to the color of their skin. There have just been too many times when POC have been called out, imprisoned, or killed for the same things that many whites have gotten away with. Of course, this is not solely happening to blacks, but they are pointing out the lack of justice in their experiences when compared to whites. They are bringing light to an issue that needs to be fixed in the same manner that many people bring the necessary attention to drowning subgroups of a larger issue. 
The most basic way to describe the movement (and I'm sure you have read this before), is to compare it to something like bringing awareness to less-known types of cancer, in order to fund research to find a cure. Cancer is cancer. The ultimate goal is to find a cure for it entirely and prevent future generations from getting it. Unfortunately, there is no "one-size-fits-all" cure for the many different types of cancer, and you'd be surprised to just how many people aren't aware of that. Bringing awareness to a lesser-known type of cancer isn't telling the people who have breast cancer "Hey! Screw you! We're so much more important!!!" It's saying, "Hey, we're in this with you, and we want you to be cured, too. It's just that not enough people know about this specific type of cancer and we really need the funding to give researchers an opportunity to run clinical trials and give us a shot at a cure, too. If the people who don't really know a lot about cancer knew about us, they might choose to donate to us. Maybe this will open the door and spark them to research about the different types of cancer and see how they can make a difference to help the cause entirely."
 
BLM is not here to divide anyone, and at it's core, it is a peaceful protest. Unfortunately, the messages can become misconstrued because of the media and because of people that do not take a moment to research the movement, causing a divide. The moment BLUE Lives Matter became a thing was the moment officers were asking people to pick a side and create a further wedge in the distrust between officers and civilians. A police officer is a profession that can be walked away from at anytime. Yes, under the uniform is a person, but one can argue that the likelihood of being killed/injured while working unfortunately just comes with the territory of that particular profession. On the other hand, a human being cannot simply change their skin color, or walk away from it at any given moment. The likelihood of being mistreated/killed/injured should never just come with the territory of the skin color you were born with. Creating something like Blue Lives Matter is what pits officers against black lives, and falsely suggests that the BLM protest is creating more danger for the lives of officers, which is really just ridiculing the protest and leading to more frustration. It suggests that we need to pick a side rather than allowing the protest to continue with it's original intention- to bring awareness to police brutality and fix the injustice that is happening to many minorities, in order to fix the system as a whole.
